questions.question: Orient verdicts for BK-504: BK-505 constrains it (it decides which further record checks and which stopping rule bind, so BK-504 builds only R1's table check), BK-506 constrains it (its S⁺ needs G3 on a spec's tables, and it runs on the freeze R2 writes into the skills), and BK-485 constrains it (the OP-01 reopen is BK-485's, so BK-504 writes its OP-01 findings as open items and decides none). What should BK-504's scope be?

options.label: As framed (Recommended)
options.description: Script with record and spec modes, tests, a domain-declaration form, a G3 step in /observe-review, R2's freeze written into /observe and /observe-review. Run on OP-01 with evidence it can fail, and write what holds as open items O45 onward in OP-01 for the reopen. Spec mode is tested on a fixture only. No freeze tag, no reopen.

options.label: Tool only, no OP-01 items
options.description: Same script and skill text, and the OP-01 run's result goes into the trace and PR only. A separate /observe-review run later writes the open items. The reopen then waits for that run.

options.label: Wider: also specs 052/053
options.description: As framed, and spec mode also runs on specs 052 and 053, filing what it finds. That means more findings outside the record flow, and a spec table may need its own domain declarations added to ground files.

questions.question: The record-quality report suggests that BK-504's OP-01 run also does two independent extractions of the record plus a blind restatement of each claim, scored against O14 to O44. Where does that measurement belong?

options.label: BK-505's input (Recommended)
options.description: It is evidence for BK-505's decision on which further checks bind, not part of R1. Record it in BK-505's entry as an open measurement. No new item, and BK-504 stays the table check.

options.label: Inside BK-504
options.description: Run it here beside the table check. That roughly doubles the work, mixes an LLM-judged measurement into a deterministic-check item, and makes the scoring scripts land here.

options.label: New backlog item
options.description: File a separate item for the measurement, sequenced before BK-505 decides.

questions.question: BK-504's open decision: how does a table in an /observe record (and later a spec) declare the domain the check ranges it over? OP-01's tables declare none today, and RFC-0028 P3 forbids /observe-review to edit a decision, so the pre-reopen run cannot add declarations to the record itself.

options.label: Sidecar file (Recommended)
options.description: One TOML file per checked document, e.g. sdd/observe/tables/OP-01.toml. Each entry anchors a table by heading and position, gives its kind (case or state), its key column and its domain members, and names the enumeration the members come from (Environment, D34's category column). The check also verifies that each member appears in that source, and any table without a declaration is a finding. Records are never edited, which works on OP-01 before the reopen and on a spec the same way. Amendments never rewrite earlier text, so the anchors stay stable.
options.preview:
[[table]]
at = "OP-01/D38"      # heading prefix
kind = "case"
key = 1
source = "OP-01/D34 column 2"
members = ["key refused", "not found",
  "not an item", ..., "cancellation"]

[[table]]
at = "OP-01/D18"
kind = "state"
states = ["Open","Exhausted","Failed","Closed"]
events = ["read","close","lifetime ends",
          "cancelled"]

options.label: Inline Domain line
options.description: The /observe session writes a fixed-form '- **Domain:**' line under each table and asks for it in the dialog (axes.md's per-question form gains it). This keeps one source with the decision. OP-01 has none, though, so the pre-reopen run can only report 'undeclared' per table, and the substantive check waits for the reopen to add the lines by amendment.
options.preview:
| Failure | A new call |
|---|---|
| ... |

- **Domain:** Failure over OP-01/D34's
  Category column

options.label: Inline, sidecar for old
options.description: Inline lines for tables written from now on, and a sidecar only for tables that predate the form (OP-01's). The check supports both forms, with two places to look.

questions.question: Should the table check gate (lint/CI) or stay advisory like observe-dialogs? DRIFT-RULES Rule 5 prefers a mandatory path and asks for the reason when a check is advisory.

options.label: Advisory (Recommended)
options.description: Run by /observe-review only, wired as 'hatch run observe-tables' in no bundle. The reason goes in its docstring and the pyproject comment: its findings are open items that only a reopen session decides, so a gate would stay red on master until each reopen. Tests run in the suite.

options.label: Gate structure only
options.description: Advisory for gaps and overlaps, but a --structure mode in lint fails on sidecar drift: an anchor not found, an undeclared table, or a member missing from its source. That catches drift between a record and its declarations at every PR, at the cost of one more flag and a lint entry.
